title: The postcard run, i
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Chloe's postcards as strips. The strip redraws her handwriting. Wood's replies are never shown.

panels.composition: The corkboard. Five postcards now, pinned photo-out. WOOD adding a sixth: a Chicago skyline.

image.prompt: a young man pinning a sixth postcard, a city skyline, to a corkboard already holding five, all photo-side out, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: The back of the Chicago card, redrawn in the strip in her tiny capitals — the whole panel is her handwriting: 'W — Chicago. Guerrilla theater in a parking garage, level 3. They performed Chekhov to a Honda. The Honda wept. You would have — no. You wouldn't have come. — C.'

image.prompt: a whole panel that is the back of a postcard covered in tiny cramped handwritten capitals, redrawn in ink
image.notes: Letter the text after; it's the panel.

panels.composition: Wood at the table with a blank postcard of the bay. The pen. The dog.

image.prompt: a young man holding a pen over a blank postcard of a bay at his drawing table, a dog under it

panels.composition: The card going into the mailbox slot. Written side hidden. As always.

image.prompt: close-up of a hand sliding a postcard into a mailbox slot with its written side hidden, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: The Postcard Run begins. Her side of the correspondence is the strip; his is never shown.
